newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 8.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Taxpayers still face a huge bill for super: Taxpayers will still foot a huge bill to top up funds in the proposed compulsory superannuation scheme -- eventually half as much again as they will save for themselves. Page 1.

Existing savings will not automatically count: Savings in existing superannuation schemes will not automatically count toward the $120,000 each person will be expected to save if the compulsory scheme is adopted. Page 1.

Agriculture, forestry merger approval tipped: An announcement on whether the agriculture and forestry ministries would merge was expected this week from the minister of both portfolios, Lockwood Smith, a spokesman for Dr Smith said on Monday. Page 1.
Kirton spends $100,000 on advice: Associate Health Minister Neil Kirton has spent more than $100,000 on consultants since the end of last year, averaging $3611 a week, figures show. Page 2.

Cabinet orders rabbit control study: The Cabinet has asked officials to assess rabbit control options for the government, after an application to import the rabbit-killing calicivirus disease was turned down last Wednesday. Page 2.

Beehive idea not debated at Cabinet: Plans to move the Beehive and complete the original Parliament buildings were not discussed at Monday's Cabinet meeting as expected, but the plans must be decided within the next month. Page 2.

Asian share reduction an option -- Wu: Asian Properties' proposed share reduction could still proceed without the sale of the company's share of Malaysian President Hotel, company director Douglas Wu said on Monday. Page 13.
Thistle earnings growth forecasts lowered: Merrill Lynch has lowered its earnings growth forecasts for Thistle Hotels, the British hotel company 46 percent owned by Brierley Investments. Page 13.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Savings impact 'will take time': It will take around three years for the newly proposed compulsory Retirement Savings Scheme to start having a real impact on financial markets, fund managers estimated on Monday.
Electronic commerce 'outstrips' laws: The Ministry of Consumer Affairs believes formal government regulations are out of place in the fast-expanding electronic marketplace.
End of company schemes 'likely': The Employers' Federation has warned that the government's proposal for a compulsory superannuation scheme could lead to many companies winding-up their own schemes.

Dairy Board rejects Luxton proposal for restructuring: The Dairy Board has been accused of being political rather than open-minded in considering a second proposal for structural change after criticising a plan put forward by the Associate Minister of Agriculture, John Luxton.

Prosecutor: Phillips knew rules: Former Kerridge executive chairman David Phillips was prepared to take advantage of such formality as existed within the group "to effect his dishonesty", prosecution Lyn Stevens QC said in closing submissions at the fraud trial on Monday.
THE PRESS
Falling dollar brings relief for exporters: The New Zealand dollar continued to fall on Monday amid billion-dollar activity and speculation on the finance markets. Page 35.
SunAlliance adds royal: Insurance company Sun Alliance became Royal SunAlliance on Monday. Page 35.
GAP signs up 300th member: GAP, New Zealand's and now Australasia's largest business group for gay and lesbian professionals, now has 300 members. Page 35.
--Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
